Count 16 equal intervals from 1/5 to 1/3. From the text, the target fraction is 1/4. Compute the numerical span: 1/3 - 1/5 = 2/15. Since this span is divided into 16 equal intervals, one tick interval represents (2/15)/16 = 1/120. Then 1/4 - 1/5 = 1/20 = 6/120, so 1/4 is 6 tick intervals to the right of 1/5. In the image, the tick 6 intervals to the right of 1/5 is labeled a.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the labels a, b, c, d, e are on consecutive interior ticks between the left tick labeled 1/5 and the right tick labeled 1/3. Instead of finding the value of each tick, compare distance ratios. From the text, the desired point is 1/4. Compute its distances from the two placed fractions: 1/4 - 1/5 = 1/20 and 1/3 - 1/4 = 1/12. The ratio of left distance to right distance is (1/20):(1/12) = 3:5. Now check the labeled positions visually by counting intervals to the endpoints. At a, there are 6 intervals back to 1/5 and 10 intervals forward to 1/3, giving 6:10 = 3:5. Therefore 1/4 should be placed at a.
